brief: 6 books that quietly changed how I run a company. Why each one mattered.

slots.headline: Six Books That Quietly Changed How I Lead

slots.title: The Effective Executive
slots.body: Drucker taught me that effectiveness is a practice, not a personality. I stopped glorifying busywork and started protecting deep-thinking time for the team. It reshaped our entire operating rhythm.

slots.title: High Output Management
slots.body: Grove showed me that a manager's output is the output of their team. I began measuring my impact by the multipliers I enabled, not tasks I completed. That shift alone changed every hiring decision.

slots.title: Turn the Ship Around
slots.body: Marquet's leader-leader model replaced my instinct to command with a habit of delegating intent. Crew members became owners, and our decision speed tripled without sacrificing clarity. Trust became our competitive advantage.

slots.title: Thinking in Bets
slots.body: Duke taught me to separate decision quality from outcome luck. We now review process, not just results, which calmed our blame culture and sped up honest post-mortems. Clarity replaced hindsight bias.

slots.title: Radical Candor
slots.body: Scott gave me language for caring personally while challenging directly. I stopped avoiding hard conversations, and my team finally got the feedback they needed to grow. Silence is not kindness.

slots.title: The Infinite Game
slots.body: Sinek reminded me that no business truly wins; it only stays in play. I moved from beating competitors to outlasting them through purpose and resilient culture. The goal is continuity, not conquest.
